People & perspectives study · Maps to Course 09 (Leadership & Org Behavior — succession, span of control, internal vs external hires), E1 (Leading at Scale — leading other leaders through a merger and a reorg), E4 (Corporate Governance & The Board — the board as succession engine, chair rotation, ex-target directors), E7 (Exec Presence & Comms — Peterson vs Cheung voice, house phrases), E12 (Culture as Strategy — "People Forward", purpose officer abolished) · Written 2026-10-25 · Part of spglobal hub; companions spglobal outside voices, spglobal mission forces, spglobal ihs markit merger

  • Source: _ingest/raw/spglobal/articles.jsonl. That is 492 items, Jan 2019 – Oct 23 2026: S&P Global press and IR releases, the chairman/CEO letters from the 2019–2025 annual reports, and the Investor Day 2022 and 2025 decks. Every appointment, departure and board release was read in full. Quotes are verbatim and dated by release date. Annual-report letters are dated by the year they describe. There are no earnings-call transcripts and no third-party press in the corpus. Every voice below is one S&P chose to print. Pronouns follow the releases (Ms. Cheung, Ms. Clay, Ms. Moore; Mr. Peterson, Mr. Saha and others). Where a release gives none, this note uses names or they.
  • Core claim: The top handover was textbook. The board "unanimously elected" Martina Cheung in June 2024. She took over in November. Doug Peterson stayed as adviser to the end of 2025 and the chair rotated six months later. Cheung was a 14-year insider. She had run Market Intelligence (MI) and Ratings, led ESG, and served as Chief Strategy Officer. Underneath, the leadership bench turned over almost completely in two years:
  • a CFO gap filled by an interim for a year;
  • three MI leaders in two years, then MI split between two co-heads;
  • new heads at S&P DJI and Mobility in 2025;
  • a new Chief Technology & Transformation Officer and Chief Legal Officer in 2026;
  • the Chief Purpose Officer role abolished. The pattern started earlier. In the 2020 merger structure, the acquirer gave its data division (MI) to the target's executive, Adam Kansler. S&P's own MI head, Cheung, went to Ratings. The detour put her on the path to CEO.

What the chart says. - The CEO handover was the one seat run like a relay. The board named a successor (Jun 27 2024). The heir joined the board on Jul 1 and took over on Nov 1. The predecessor kept a board seat until May 2025 and an adviser role to Dec 31 2025. The chair who ran the process (Thornburgh) then handed over too. - The CFO seat had the opposite pattern. On Dec 7 2023 Steenbergen's exit was announced with about three months' notice "to pursue another professional opportunity". No successor was named. Craig, the Chief Accounting Officer, held it for about a year while "internal and external CFO candidates" were evaluated. The gap overlapped the CEO change. - MI is the hot spot. Cheung (to 2021), then Kansler (2022–Oct 2024), then Saha (Nov 2024–Jul 2026), then two co-heads. That is three leaders and one split in under five years, and two leaders plus the split in two years. - Insiders run the core; outsiders fill new capabilities. Insiders: Cheung, Le Pallec (joined Ratings 1999), Ernsberger (joined Platts 1996), Saha, Craig, Eager (20+ years at CARFAX). Outsiders: Aboaf (State Street), Bhathena (FIS), Kim (Gartner and Thomson Reuters), Clay (Cboe). Every one of those outsiders arrived in 2025–26. - The target supplied leaders. IHS Markit people got MI (Kansler), Mobility (Tavernier), Vice Chair (Yergin), four board seats, and later Chief Client Officer (Moore, from Markit). Its CEO, Lance Uggla, stayed one year as special adviser.

2. Profiles

Douglas L. Peterson — CEO 2013 – Oct 2024

Background: joined in 2011 as President of Ratings ("rebuilt trust in the ratings agency", per his 2024 bio). Talks about: demand rising in crises, scale, "powering markets", AI inside existing franchises. - Crises raise demand. "The demand for our ratings, benchmarks, research, data, and analytics is greater than ever during uncertain and volatile markets," (Oct 27 2020). And in 2019: "We don't let market disruptions interfere with our business plans." (May 2 2019, in a quarter when Ratings revenue fell 7%). - Scale is the strategy. "This merger increases scale while rounding out our combined capabilities" (Nov 30 2020). - Optimism that misfired once. The 2021 letter says "As great as last year was for our company, in many ways 2022 is shaping up to be even better." The 2022 letter admits "our financial performance in 2022 did not match the previous year." - AI as a natural extension. "Generative AI was one of the biggest global news stories last year. It’s really a game changer." (2023 letter). - On his own exit: "The Board and I have had a robust succession process in place for many years, and now is the ideal time for this transition." (Jun 27 2024). - Record, as S&P states it (Jun 27 2024): revenue $4.45B → $12.50B; adjusted EPS $2.75 → $12.60; more than $30B returned; market cap $16B → over $135B.

Martina L. Cheung — CEO from Nov 1 2024

Path: joined 2010 as VP Operations, Ratings → Chief Strategy Officer → Head of Risk Services, MI → President of MI (to 2021; "the division exceeded $2 billion in annual revenue") → Head of the ESG team (Dec 2020) and Sustainable1 sponsor → President of Ratings (Feb 2022) → CEO. The succession release also credits her as "instrumental" in the SNL (2015) and IHS Markit (2022) deals. Talks about: data and technology serving the customer, then AI raising the value of proprietary data, then "trusted, connected" data. - 2020 (running MI): "Technology and data science are playing a crucial role in how we bring value to our customers," (May 14 2020). - 2021 (ESG peak): "The launch of S&P Global Sustainable1 signifies the critical intersection between sustainability and business performance" (Apr 22 2021). - 2024 (first letter as CEO): "I didn’t know you do that, too." She says CEOs often told her this, and she uses it as the reason for the Chief Client Office. Also: "GenAI will have profound and accelerating effects across all sectors of the economy and in society." - 2025: "Separating Mobility will allow us to continue to focus on our core businesses and pursue our growth strategy," (Apr 29 2025). And "we are seeing more tailwinds than headwinds." (2025 letter). - 2026: "In a world where data is abundant, but not all created equal, customers need trusted, connected, essential intelligence that brings context and conviction to decision-making" (Jul 6 2026). In the same release: "These changes within Market Intelligence align our capabilities, enabling us to elevate the customer experience while growing our revenue and improving margins." - Culture line: "One of the first things I did as CEO was to affirm my commitment to fostering a culture where our people feel valued." (2024 letter). She calls it the People Forward philosophy.

Richard E. (Dick) Thornburgh — director 2011–25, Chair Oct 2020 – May 2025

Ex-Credit Suisse CFO and CRO. Chaired the board through the merger and the CEO selection. - On his appointment (Sep 30 2020), the release says the board was overseeing a move "from a conglomerate to an operating company model." - On Peterson: "Doug led the evolution of our Company from a diversified publishing holding company to a focused, markets-oriented information services company." (Jun 27 2024). And: "He was bold while remaining humble." (2024 letter). - On Cheung: "Martina is the right leader to take the baton from Doug and lead S&P Global." (2024 letter).

Ian P. Livingston — Chair from May 7 2025

Director since 2020. Ex-CEO and CFO of BT Group, ex-UK trade minister. - "In a fast-changing world, S&P Global's mission to provide Essential Intelligence has never been more important." (Mar 25 2025). - On AI: "the growth of artificial intelligence, which provides significant opportunities for the business and some potential challenges." (2025 letter). He names blockchain and quantum computing as other areas the board is watching.

Ewout Steenbergen — CFO Nov 2016 – Mar 2024

Credited with the Kensho deal, the IHS Markit merger, climate-adjusted EPS and the Vitality Index. Also ran Engineering Solutions before it was sold in 2023. - "I have full confidence in the future of the company." (Dec 7 2023, the exit release). - ESG voice in 2021: "Linking our line of credit to SBTi-verified targets makes tangible S&P Global's commitment to becoming net-zero by 2040," (Apr 26 2021).

Christopher Craig (interim CFO 2024–25) and Eric Aboaf (CFO from Feb 2025)

  • Craig: Chief Accounting Officer, 13+ years at the company. Peterson: "Chris has been instrumental in developing our financial management strategy" (Feb 2 2024). No public quote from Craig.
  • Aboaf: CFO of State Street for nearly eight years; earlier Citizens and Citi Treasurer. He was also given Strategy, M&A and Ventures, a scope taken from Moore. Cheung praised his "deep understanding of the markets and regulatory landscape in which we operate" (Oct 15 2024). There is no Aboaf quote in the corpus. He presented the financial targets at Investor Day 2025.

Adam Kansler — President of MI, Feb 2022 – Oct 2024

Was IHS Markit's President of Financial Services, and named to run the combined MI on Dec 16 2020. - "We are highly disciplined in reviewing our businesses and focusing our investment in our core areas of growth." (Feb 20 2024: buying Visible Alpha while exploring a sale of Fincentric). - 2023 on private markets: "the scale of private market financing has reached a point where knowledge of these markets is essential." (Apr 18 2023). - Replaced eight months after the Visible Alpha quote. Special adviser to March 2025.

Saugata Saha — Platts/Commodity Insights 2021–24, MI and Chief Enterprise Data Officer 2024–26

Ex-McKinsey. Was CFO of MI and of Platts, and ran FP&A and corporate strategy. The release credits his Commodity Insights years with "growing annual revenue by 10% since the merger". - "The expansion of private credit and the emergence of secondary trading necessitates common identifiers," (Jun 24 2025). - "Data consumption is not one-size-fits-all; our customers require sophisticated, AI-enabled solutions" (Jul 17 2025). - Left Jul 30 2026 "to pursue another opportunity". Instead of naming a new MI president, the company split MI and moved the Enterprise Data Organization under the CTTO.

Sally Moore — Strategy/M&A → Chief Client Officer (Nov 2024) → MI co-head (Jul 2026)

Joined Markit in 2006 and ran its European credit and global loan businesses. Before that, Thomson Reuters LPC. - "We've heard from our clients that fragmented data and inconsistent reporting standards are creating operational inefficiencies" (Sep 15 2025). - "The use of AI in financial services is rapidly accelerating and evolving, from tightly controlled workflows to fully autonomous, multi-agent systems" (Jul 21 2026). - "We are meeting clients where they work, embedding S&P Global's trusted, high-quality data directly into their workflows" (Aug 12 2026).

Darren Thomas — Head of Lending Solutions → Enterprise Solutions → MI co-head and ELT (Jul 2026)

  • "agents are still managing billion-dollar deals with Excel and email, creating massive operational risk" (Mar 3 2026).
  • Pricing and reference data now sit in this vertical. See spglobal pricing fixed income.

Bhavesh Dayalji (Kensho), Swamy Kocherlakota (digital) and Firdaus Bhathena (CTTO)

  • Dayalji: CEO of Kensho, and Chief AI Officer from late 2023. On Jul 6 2026 the title became "Head of Kensho Data & Intelligence". Main lines: "we want to make our data more easily and immediately accessible to the entire LLM ecosystem," (Nov 13 2024). "S&P Global is committed to meeting our customers where their workflows take place," (Jul 15 2025). "For S&P Global, the data retrieval layer is only the beginning." (Jul 21 2026).
  • Kocherlakota: CIO, then Chief Digital Solutions Officer and sponsor of AI and Kensho (late 2023). Previously Visa and BNY Mellon. "AI is undeniably accelerating progress and driving transformative change across various sectors," (Dec 4 2024). Kocherlakota is not named in any 2026 release in the corpus, and the 2026 technology structure puts Bhathena on top.
  • Bhathena: a new role, effective Apr 27 2026. Previously FIS Global CTO (24,000 staff) and CVS Health. "build a world-class, unified technology engine that harnesses the full power of data and AI" (Mar 31 2026). The data organization moved under Bhathena eight weeks later.

Dan Draper → Catherine Clay (S&P Dow Jones Indices) and Cameron Drinkwater (product)

  • Draper (Jun 2020 – Oct 2025; ex-Invesco ETFs): independent index provider is the recurring line. "One of S&P DJI's key priorities as an independent index provider is to continue offering choice to the market." (Sep 16 2024). On Sep 8 2025 Draper was the voice of the IOSCO review. The appointment of a replacement was announced 24 days later.
  • Clay (from Nov 2025): ex-Cboe Global Head of Derivatives and Data Vantage; earlier CEO of LiveVol. "excited to lead a team that is at the forefront of building trusted benchmarks for every investor." (Oct 2 2025). In 2026: "As digital assets accelerate S&P Global is investing for the future—and this investment underscores that conviction" (Sep 14 2026, Kaiko).
  • Drinkwater (Chief Product, later Chief Product & Operations Officer): the voice of DJI's on-chain launches. "We believe digitally-native investors should demand the institutional-quality standards that define our indices" (Mar 18 2026). See spglobal indices benchmarks and spglobal digital assets.

Yann Le Pallec — President of Ratings from Nov 2024

Joined Ratings in 1999. Ran Global Ratings Services (2,200+ staff, 28 countries) and chaired CRISIL. - On taking the job, he aims to "build on the analytical excellence and transparency that are synonymous with our ratings agency" (Jun 27 2024). - In 2026: "Our digital assets strategy centers on bringing trusted data, benchmarks and transparent risk assessment to markets as they move onchain" (Sep 17 2026, OpenZeppelin). And: "Africa's opportunity is extraordinary" (Jul 28 2026, Agusto).

Dave Ernsberger — Platts since 1996 → Commodity Insights co-President (2024) → S&P Global Energy

  • "AI is transforming not only technology markets, but the physical infrastructure and energy systems that underpin the global economy" (Jul 28 2026, datacenterHawk).
  • In 2024 the line was still energy transition: "We are especially delighted to observe the growing adoption of our energy transition-focused commodity prices" (Jun 27 2024).

Daniel Yergin — Vice Chairman (from IHS Markit, 2022–)

The CERAWeek host and the company's most quoted outside-facing intellectual. - "the energy future must be secure and affordable, as well as sustainable." (Dec 21 2022). - "Expectations of a linear path to Net-zero are giving way to recognition that this will be a multidimensional energy transition" (Feb 26 2024). - "The race for AI is fusing the energy and technology industries like never before" (Feb 17 2026). These lines run ahead of the company's own retreat from ESG language. See spglobal esg reversal.

Chuck Mounts — Chief DeFi Officer (Ratings, from May 2022)

  • "The launch of SSAs on-chain through Chainlink underscores our commitment to meeting our clients where they are," (Oct 14 2025).

Steve Kemps → Thomas Kim (Chief Legal Officer)

  • Kemps: CLO since 2016. In 2024 the remit grew to Compliance and Risk. Retiring at the end of 2026: "I am incredibly proud of what we've accomplished together" (Jul 6 2026).
  • Kim: previously CLO of Gartner (2023–) and of Thomson Reuters (2019–23). The release says Kim "led the separation of the $6 billion financial and risk data division (now a part of the London Stock Exchange)". That division is Refinitiv, which controlled Tradeweb. See lseg hub and thomsonreuters hub.

Edouard Tavernier → Bill Eager (Mobility)

  • Tavernier ran the IHS Markit Transportation unit, then Mobility for 12 years. "Our team has played an important role in bringing transparency to the industry" (Jul 31 2025).
  • Eager (CARFAX for 20+ years; its CEO from 2021): "We have a terrific runway ahead for growth and innovation," (Jul 31 2025). Became CEO of Mobility Global at the Jul 1 2026 spin.

Lance Uggla — IHS Markit Chairman & CEO; special adviser one year after close

  • "This transaction is a win for both IHS Markit and S&P Global" (Nov 30 2020).
  • "Our cultures are well aligned, and the combined company will provide greater career opportunities for employees." (Nov 30 2020).

3. Where leaders' perspectives differ or shift

Issue Earlier view (who, when) Later / contrasting view (who, when) Read
Breadth vs focus Peterson: the merger "increases scale while rounding out our combined capabilities" (2020). The six-division company at the 2022 close Cheung: Mobility out to "focus on our core businesses" (2025). Kansler: "highly disciplined in reviewing our businesses" (2024). Sales of Engineering Solutions, Fincentric, PrimeOne, OSTTRA, EDM/thinkFolio and upstream software The Peterson strategy added; the Cheung strategy subtracts. Kansler's 2024 line is the hinge
AI: cost → product → channel 2019–20 earnings treat Kensho as margin drag and "retention-related expenses". Peterson calls Kensho the AI business "we acquired in 2018" Dayalji: data for "the entire LLM ecosystem" (2024). Cheung: AI makes proprietary data more valuable (2025). In 2026 Kensho names half of MI The firm moved from building AI to supplying AI. See spglobal ai data layer
ESG / energy Cheung: Sustainable1 at "the critical intersection" (2021). Steenbergen: net-zero 2040 (2021) Yergin: no "linear path" (2024). Cheung: "energy expansion, not replacement" (2025 letter). Sustainable1 folded (Oct 2024) The same executive built the franchise and folded it. See spglobal esg reversal
What an index provider is Matturri: "Our philosophy as an independent index provider is to offer choice to investors." (2019) Clay: the mission bridges "traditional and decentralized finance" (2026). Drinkwater: indices on Hyperliquid and Canton From a neutral administrator to a licensor following liquidity wherever it trades
Optimism about the cycle Peterson: 2022 "shaping up to be even better" (2021 letter) 2022: guidance suspended (Jun 1), revenue down 4% pro forma. Peterson: performance "did not match the previous year" The CEO underestimated Ratings' exposure to issuance
Who owns the customer Divisions own their clients (2019–23) Cheung's Chief Client Office (2024). Moore: "meeting clients where they work" (2026) Account ownership centralised; divisions become product lines

The three sharpest shifts: (1) Peterson to Cheung: from adding scale to subtracting assets. (2) Kensho: from cost centre to the brand of half of MI. (3) ESG: from Cheung's flagship (2021) to a folded unit (2024).

4. Communication style and narrative craft

Peterson: the macro statesman. He opens with the world ("two wars, the polarization of politics"), ties it to demand, then lists metrics. His slogans are strategic frames, not products: Powering the Markets of the Future, then Powering Global Markets. He admits weakness once ("did not match") and reframes it in the same sentence as discipline.

Cheung: the operator-integrator. Her slogans are about structure: Chief Client Office, Enterprise Data Organization, CTTO, People Forward. She likes anecdotes from customers ("I didn’t know you do that, too."). Her strategy is stated as three objectives and every release maps to one. She names margin openly. "improving margins" is in the July 2026 reorg quote, where Peterson-era releases would have said growth.

House phrases and first sightings: - essential intelligence: boilerplate from 2019. A capitalised brand by 2025 (Livingston). - make decisions with conviction: corporate wording. The divisions still say confidence in 2026. - power(ing) the markets of the future (2019–21) → powering global markets (2022–24) → Advancing Essential Intelligence (2025–). - meeting customers where they are / where their workflows take place: Dayalji, Mounts, Eramo, Moore, 2025–26. - trusted: the most frequent adjective in 2026 AI and digital-asset releases.

What they never talk about: - Why each of these left: Steenbergen, Kansler, Saha, Draper, Tavernier. - The pricing business and the MarketAxess deal after October 2024. - Fee levels, client churn and headcount after the merger (the 2025 chairman letter gives "more than 40,000 people"). - Analysts' questions (the corpus has no call transcripts).

5. Culture and talent, as the leaders describe it

  • Values change with the merger. In 2019 the values were excellence, relevance, integrity (2019 letter). The 2021 merger letter adds new values, discovery, partnership, integrity. The purpose is "Accelerate Progress" (2023, O'Hanlon: "Our company's purpose – to accelerate progress –").
  • Purpose function downgraded. The Chief Purpose Officer (Manis) left in Oct 2024 and the role was not refilled. Corporate Responsibility disclosures moved under the CFO.
  • People function upgraded. Girish Ganesan became Chief People Officer (2024). Mandatory "AI for Everyone" training followed (2025), and StepForward ($10M, Dec 2025): "StepForward extends our People Forward philosophy into global communities".
  • Integration as culture. IHS Markit brought over 15,000 people (2024 letter). Ex-target executives held MI, Mobility and the Vice Chair seat. Board town halls ("1,500 employees" at the Javits Center, 2023 chairman letter) are the board's culture check.
  • Absent: attrition, return-to-office, integration friction, and why the President role in MI stayed empty after Saha.

6. Leadership lenses

  • canon kotter leading change: the CEO change shows Kotter's guiding coalition. There was a public plan, a long overlap and a named successor. The MI reorg shows the opposite: a sudden exit, "We expect to move quickly", and a structure in place of a person.
  • canon grove high output management: Cheung's structural moves (CCO, EDO, CTTO) are Grove's managerial leverage. Each one is a lever affecting many divisions. The cost is a thinner bench of division presidents.
  • canon pfeffer power: power moved from divisions to enterprise functions (client, data, technology). Watch who reports to whom. The EDO moved from the MI president to the CTTO in eight weeks.
  • canon schein organizational culture: the artifacts are People Forward, Spark Assist and the town halls. The espoused value is "Essential Intelligence". The basic assumption is that the data is the moat. The 2026 Farsight quote (spglobal outside voices) challenges exactly that assumption.
  • canon drucker effective executive: Drucker's first things first. Cheung's first year was subtraction (Mobility, OSTTRA, software sales) before addition (With Intelligence).
  • canon bezos shareholder letters: the S&P letters re-theme every year ("Resilience", "Uncertain World, Discover Opportunity", "Let’s Unlock Potential Together"). Unlike Bezos, they never re-attach or score earlier promises. The ESG targets of 2021–22 are never revisited by name.
  • canon heath switch: the CCO "I didn’t know you do that, too." anecdote is Heath's find the bright spots / shape the path. Customers did not know the catalogue, so the change is in go-to-market, not product.

Part A (E4, numbers). You sit on S&P's Nominating & Governance Committee in 2027. Score the 2023–26 leadership record with these figures from §1: - CFO gap: Steenbergen's exit was announced Dec 7 2023 and Aboaf started Feb 2025. (Answer: about 14 months from announcement to permanent CFO, about 12 of them with an interim.) - MI tenure: Kansler Feb 2022 – Oct 2024 (~32 months); Saha Nov 2024 – Jul 2026 (~21 months). Average tenure? (Answer: ~26.5 months.) Compare Peterson's ~11 years as CEO. - Outside hires in the executive leadership team, 2025–26: Aboaf, Clay, Bhathena, Kim. Out of roughly 12–14 ELT seats, what share turned over to outsiders in 18 months? (Answer: 4/13 ≈ 31%.)

Then write three questions for the CEO's 2027 review: one on the MI structure, one on the bench, one on why the data organization moved twice.

Part B (E7). Rewrite Cheung's Jul 6 2026 MI-reorg quote in Peterson's 2020 voice: macro opener, demand claim, scale. Then say which version an analyst would trust more on margins, and why.
